quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: If someone is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
In the center of the lane.
On the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is the safest place to ride when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding on the far side can make the driver return to your lane too quickly.

questions.question: What gear should your motorcycle be in when you start the engine?
questions.explanation: Always put your motorcycle in neutral before starting the engine. Most motorcycles have a neutral light on the speedometer that shows when the engine is on and in neutral.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the signal will change to red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, keep going.

questions.question: Is eye protection required for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Eye protection is required by law for all motorcycle riders in Georgia.

questions.question: Which surface is most likely to be slippery?
questions.explanation: Gravel roads, wet pavement, snow, ice, mud, lane markings, and metal utility covers all have poor traction and can be slippery.

questions.question: How should your arms be positioned when holding the handlebars?
questions.explanation: Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handlebars. This reduces fatigue and lets you press on the bars without stretching too far.

questions.question: Where is there the most risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles?
questions.explanation: Intersections have the highest risk of conflict between motorcycles and other vehicles. Always be careful when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: What material should riding gloves be made of?
questions.explanation: Riding gloves should be made of leather or a similar tough material to give you the best grip and protection.

questions.question: What should a rider do in high-risk areas?

options.text: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brake levers to react faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brake levers to react faster.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping areas, schools, and construction zones, slow down. Keep your hands ready on the clutch and both brake levers so you can react quickly to emergencies.

questions.question: How fast does your body remove alcohol?
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour on average. This varies by person. The safest choice is to not ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: To make it easier for other drivers to see you, you should:
questions.explanation: Bright-colored clothing makes you easier to see on the road. This works any time of day.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride faster than you normally would.
Start slowing down earlier than you normally would.
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than you normally would.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than you normally would.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. This extra weight makes the motorcycle slower to respond when you speed up, slow down, or turn. Because of this, slow down sooner, begin braking earlier, and look for larger gaps in traffic when crossing or merging.

questions.question: When riding, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Be loose enough so wind can catch the fabric.
Fit snug enough to not flap in the wind.
Be tight enough to stop you from moving freely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snug enough to not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should fit snug so they do not flap in the wind, but loose enough so you can move freely.

questions.question: For motorcycle riders, helmets are:
questions.explanation: In Georgia, you must wear a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards every time you ride a motorcycle.

questions.question: When carrying a load, it should be:
questions.explanation: Loads should be secured low to keep your motorcycle balanced.

questions.question: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because:

options.text: The front tire affects steering and balance.
A flat front tire will disable the front brake.
A flat front tire will stop you from speeding up.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front tire affects steering and balance.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it affects your steering, which affects your balance. If steering feels heavy, you may have a flat front tire.

questions.question: You have a better chance of avoiding serious injury in a crash if you wear all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: A DOT-compliant helmet protects your head and neck in a crash. A leather or sturdy synthetic jacket also protects you from injuries.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: Riders under 21 are legally impaired with a minimum blood alcohol content (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: In Georgia, riders under 21 are legally impaired at 0.02 percent BAC. Riding while drunk is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, the following distance should:
questions.explanation: A motorcycle towing a trailer needs more space to stop. The extra weight means longer stopping time, so increase your following distance.
